note: Authoritative local data from L1 chains.db (DeFiLlama + CoinGecko + growthepie/Dune). Raw signals, no scores. null = NO DATA (do not guess). FRESHNESS: price & market caps are live (today); TVL/stablecoin LEVELS are the latest available (carried forward if a chain's today-point isn't in yet); daily-FLOW metrics (DEX volume, fees, active_addresses, tx_count) are the LAST COMPLETE UTC DAY (today is partial and excluded) — full-day figures, use them as-is. SHARES are each chain's % of the WHOLE DeFi market (all ~500 chains; denominators in market.total_*), so tracked chains sum to <100% and deltas are immune to which chains we track. TVL/volume are USD-denominated, so share moves in a big market swing partly reflect token price, not pure flows. Each chain ALSO carries its OWN raw TVL growth — tvl_change_1d/7d/30d_pct (chain's level vs itself N days ago); use THESE for 'is this chain's TVL growing', NOT the share deltas (share = slice of market, a different question). If tvl_suspect_1d is true the 1d move is a likely upstream data glitch (a >25% one-day swing) — discount the 1d figure and lean on the 7d/30d trend instead. Stablecoins mirror this: stable_change_1d/7d/30d_pct are the chain's OWN stablecoin-supply trend (use for 'is stablecoin capital arriving/leaving', and to confirm or debunk 'stables doubled/halved' claims); stable_suspect_1d flags a >30% one-day swing as a likely DeFiLlama adapter flap (a bridged asset dropping in/out of the index) — call it out as a data-quality event, not a capital flow, and lean on 7d/30d. N-days-ago baselines are median-smoothed, so a one-day glitch can't fake a 7d/30d trend.

emerging_candidates.how_to_use: RAW watchlist of non-radar chains rising on the signals below — NOT buy calls. A candidate becomes a LEAD only on confluence (also trending / in a heating narrative / has a catalyst / fresh dev-gov) or a confirmed on-chain TVL surge.

signal_glossary.volume_heat: Volume is large vs market cap (turnover ≥15%) — unusual interest building.
signal_glossary.vol_leads_price: Volume is hot but 7d price hasn't run yet — interest building BEFORE the move (the early sweet spot).
signal_glossary.momentum: 7d gain keeping pace with / exceeding 30d — the move is accelerating, not fading.
signal_glossary.low_float: Only a small share of supply circulates — CAUTION: unlock overhang can cap upside.
signal_glossary.tvl_surge: On-chain TVL jumped ≥25% in 7d from a small base — real capital arriving, not just token price.

pre_winner_lookalikes.method: validated winner-DNA coil screen (deep-below-high + oversold + at-30d-low [all validated, hold OOS] + below-ATH/high-vol/mid-float/small-cap); primed-but-not-yet-moved. NECESSARY-not-sufficient setup — needs an event trigger.
pre_winner_lookalikes.how_to_use: Beaten-down coils matching the data-validated winner DNA. SETUPS, not buys: most never move. Edge comes ONLY from confluence — a lookalike that is also trending / in a heating narrative / has a near catalyst / has fresh dev-gov.

signal_glossary.deep_below_60d_high: Trading <50% of its 60-day high — deeply beaten down. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.oversold_30d: Down >25% over 30 days — oversold. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.at_30d_low: Trading within ~3% of its 30-day low RIGHT NOW — the capitulation launch zone. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample); a bounce off the low actually LOWERS winner odds, so this is a timing edge.
signal_glossary.oversold_90d: Down >40% over 90 days — sustained downtrend (supporting context).
signal_glossary.deep_below_ath: Trading <15% of all-time high — far from prior peak, room to recover.
signal_glossary.high_vol: Elevated 30d volatility — capable of large moves.
signal_glossary.mid_float: Meaningful but not-fully-diluted float — the winner sweet spot.
signal_glossary.small_cap: Sub-$100M market cap — small enough to multiply.

dev_governance.note: Pre-announcement layer (early, low-crowd): GitHub releases/commit-activity + Snapshot governance for tracked protocols. A fresh_release or a pending 'launch/fund X' proposal precedes the marketing post. Each item carries release_notes / body (truncated) + a keyword dimension_hint (raw, NOT a verdict) — the FOLLOW-UP is to read these and judge what the change actually does and whether it improves the protocol at a fundamental level (consensus/scaling/security/economics/new capability) vs routine housekeeping. No composite score.

dev.release_notes:
## What's Changed
* eth/sequencer: cap coalesced published records at the store message limit by @cffls in https://github.com/0xPolygon/bor/pull/2400


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/0xPolygon/bor/compare/v2.10.2-preconf...v2.10.2-preconf2

## Protocol
#### Sui Protocol Version in this release: `136`

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27791: Adds protocol versions 135 and 136. `defer_unpaid_amplification` is disabled on mainnet at v134 and on all networks from v135; v135 also applies v134's original_package_id costs and consensus block limits on mainnet. v136 carries the previously pending v135 features.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27454: Adds `TransactionExpiration::Validity`, which restricts the transaction to a named set of consensus proposers. Behind the `allowed_proposers` feature flag, enabled on devnet only; no change on mainnet or testnet.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27451: New feature flag `ptb_tx_context_restrictions` (protocol version 135). `TxContext` in a PTB Move call signature may appear at most once as `&mut TxContext` or any number of times as `&TxContext`, never by value, and never in return position. Transactions calling functions that violate these rules now fail up front with the new `InvalidTxContext` command argument error (previously they failed with borrow-checking, arity, or serialization errors, or in dev-inspect could partially succeed).

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27832: Add additional invariant checks around packages.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27826: Adds `package_arena_size_in_bytes` (10MB, matching prior hardcoded behavior) to protocol version 136, bounding the arena a package is loaded into by the Move VM.

## Nodes …[truncated]

`v6.7.0-rc1` is the first release candidate of the `v6.7` line, cut from `release/v6.7`.

See the [`v6.7` section of the CHANGELOG](https://github.com/sei-protocol/sei-chain/blob/release/v6.7/CHANGELOG.md#v67) for the full list of changes and the upgrade guide, which covers the IBC core, transfer and query removal, the capability and feegrant module removal, the WebSocket frame-size default change, the ABCI/gRPC pagination caps, and the legacy `sei_*` JSON-RPC removal.

* [safety-paper] add reentrancy check section by @vgao1996 in …[truncated]

## Overview

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a **required release for World Chain** operators running the built-in `--chain` configs, and a **strongly recommended** one for everyone else. It contains World Chain Karst activations, a security dependency update, transaction-decoding hardening and one breaking flag removal.

Note: if you run op-rbuilder, pair this release with [op-rbuilder/v0.4.14](https://github.com/flashbots/op-rbuilder/releases/tag/op-rbuilder%2Fv0.4.14).

## Breaking changes

- **`--minimal` rejected at startup** (#22108). It was already documented as unsupported and now produces a hard startup error instead. Remove the flag before upgrading, and resync — a datadir built with it has pruned bodies and needs one anyway. The supported recipe is `--prune.minimum-distance`, `--prune.receipts.distance`, `--prune.account-history.distance` and `--prune.storage-history.distance`; do not prune block bodies.

### Chain configuration changes

- **New World Chain Karst activation times** (#22624). The embedded superchain registry gains:

  - `sepolia/worldchain` — `karst_time = 1788868800` (Tue 8 Sep 2026 12:00:00 UTC)
  - `mainnet/worldchain` — `karst_time = 1789992000` (Mon 21 Sep 2026 12:00:00 UTC)

  A World Chain node on an earlier release, running the built-in `--chain` config rather than an explicit chain config, will not activate Karst and will diverge from the chain. No other chain's activation times change in this release.

## Other Changes

### …[truncated]

This release is available as a Docker Image on Docker Hub at `offchainlabs/nitro-node:v3.11.3-beb2108`
This Docker image specifies default flags in its entrypoint which should be replicated if you're overriding the entrypoint: `/usr/local/bin/nitro --validation.wasm.allowed-wasm-module-roots /home/user/nitro-legacy/machines,/home/user/target/machines`

If you're running a validator without a split validation server (this will be true of most validators), you should instead use the image offchainlabs/nitro-node:v3.11.3-beb2108-validator which has the extra script `/usr/local/bin/split-val-entry.sh` as the entrypoint.


## [v3.11.3](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/compare/v3.11.2...v3.11.3) - 2026-08-03

### Fixed

- Capture panics on prefetch-tx execution and log them instead of returning. [[commit]](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/commit/37ea62ee48b233a71792e008246cf0163f2e0c93)
- Filter retryable submissions by who actually gets funds, and catch filtered L1 senders/depositors that previously slipped through.[[commit]](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/commit/b668bd3243c8c6392dcf86d1ae06ddccc258493d)

### Changed

- Filtered transactions rejected by the sequencer now return the RPC error message "Transaction rejected by chain policy" instead of the generic "internal error". [[commit]](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/commit/df606b3a3ae62cf19cd44f3ce54037d03400a9f0)
- Filtered-tx reports are now logged node-side when reported. Unbounded …[truncated]

## What Changed

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Base Mainnet:** Required upgrade and migration by mid August.
> **Base Sepolia:** Highly recommended upgrade and migration.
> **Migration time:** Migrations may take a while, we strongly suggest you start mainnet as soon as possible.
> **V1 Snapshots:** Will be decommissioned over the next few weeks.

### base-reth-node
- **Reth V2 Snapshots** To benefit from V2, you must both update to 1.2.0 and update your database to use v2 storage. You can do this via:
  * **Recommended:** Download a new snapshot `base-reth-node download`. See the [docs](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/node-operators/snapshots) for more information.
  * Migrate your existing V1 data `base-reth-node db migrate-v2`. Note: `migrate-v2` is expected to take **much** longer than `download`. Non-archival nodes are not supported for this command.
- **Upgrades Reth to v2.3.0**
- Bug fixes and stability improvements

### base-consensus
- **Fixed prune node sync**: Nodes can reliably do a pruned node sync from genesis
- Bug fixes and stability improvements

![image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/berachain/beacon-kit/refs/heads/main/.github/assets/banner.png)

## Summary

This release accompanies the Osaka1 EL hard fork on bepolia. Osaka1 is EL-only, so **no beacond upgrade is required for the fork**. Activation details and node upgrade instructions are in the execution client release: [bera-reth v1.4.3-rc.0](https://github.com/berachain/bera-reth/releases/tag/v1.4.3-rc.0).

This release also updates the network eth-genesis.json files with the Osaka1 schedule, bepolia activates on July 22, 2026 16:00 UTC and mainnet keeps a placeholder time for now. These files live in the repository itself and are not attached as release assets.

## Update Priority

This table provides priorities for which classes of users should update particular components.

| User Class           | Priority        |
|----------------------|-----------------|
| Payload Builders     | Optional          |
| Non-Payload Builders | Optional          |

# Abstract

The following case from the [Watchdog Program](https://alt.gov.arbitrum.foundation/proposal/28485587559812799913134094629469849411398475232393607771326861344548198896843?govId=eip155:42161:0x789fc99093b09ad01c34dc7251d0c89ce743e5a4) has been deemed to constitute high-severity misuse. Accordingly, the Watchdog Committee is proposing to ban this project from the ArbitrumDAO:

-   [APX Finance](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/apx-finance-ltipp-application-final/21744) (formerly ApolloX)
    

# Rationale

To strengthen oversight of grant allocations by the DAO and reduce misuse, the ArbitrumDAO approved the [Watchdog Program](https://alt.gov.arbitrum.foundation/proposal/28485587559812799913134094629469849411398475232393607771326861344548198896843?govId=eip155:42161:0x789fc99093b09ad01c34dc7251d0c89ce743e5a4) to reward verifiable reports of misused funds.
